basics.description: Redeploys an EXISTING Segue install onto a new application version — the minimum-steps update path (Container Apps roll a new revision on the new image tag; FHIRBridgeDb migrates automatically on boot). This targets the SAME resource group and resources as your original install, it does not create a new environment. Enter the exact same deployment name prefix, Postgres/Redis/secrets mode, storage redundancy, passwords, and API signing key you used originally — getting Postgres mode, Redis mode, secrets mode, or storage redundancy wrong doesn't just misconfigure something, it breaks connectivity or makes existing secrets unreachable (or, for storage redundancy, fails the deployment outright). Container/database/cache SIZES are still left at main.bicep's own defaults by this limited wizard (getting those wrong only under/over-provisions, it doesn't break anything) — use Step 4 (upgrade-resources) or the full Deploy-to-Azure wizard if your original install customized those.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Must match the region your original Segue install already runs in.

basics.name: namePrefix
basics.label: Existing deployment name prefix
basics.toolTip: MUST match the prefix your original install used (e.g. <prefix>-app, <prefix>-postgres) — this is what makes this an in-place update of the existing app/worker instead of a brand-new deployment.

constraints.validationMessage: Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only, starting with a letter.

options.text: Every field below MUST match your original install exactly. Postgres mode, Redis mode, and secrets mode determine which real resource (and which real secret store) the app connects to at runtime — getting any of these wrong doesn't fail the deployment, it deploys successfully and then the app can't find its database, cache, or secrets. Storage redundancy is checked at deploy time instead: Azure does not allow converting an existing storage account between Standard_LRS and Standard_ZRS at all, so picking the wrong one here fails the deployment outright (PreflightValidationCheckFailed / StorageAccountTypeConversionNotAllowed). Check the original install's parameters (or the Portal resource list) if you're unsure of any of these.

elements.name: storageRedundancy
elements.label: Storage redundancy
elements.toolTip: MUST match what your original install actually has — check the storage account's Redundancy setting in the Portal (or the resourceManifest output from your original deploy) if unsure. This cannot be changed after the storage account exists; picking the wrong value fails this deployment.

elements.name: postgresMode
elements.label: Postgres deployment type
elements.toolTip: MUST match your original install. Managed = Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Containerized = a Postgres container in this same environment.

elements.name: postgresPassword
elements.toolTip: The SAME Postgres password your original install used.

constraints.validationMessage: At least 8 characters, including upper case, lower case, and a digit.

elements.name: jwtSigningKey
elements.toolTip: The SAME API signing key your original install used — changing this invalidates every existing login session and refresh token.

elements.name: redisMode
elements.label: Redis deployment type
elements.toolTip: MUST match your original install. Containerized = a Redis container in this same environment (self-signed TLS cert). Managed = Azure Managed Redis.

elements.name: redisPassword
elements.toolTip: The SAME Redis password your original install used.

elements.name: redisTrustedCertificateThumbprint
elements.label: Redis TLS certificate thumbprint
elements.toolTip: The SAME thumbprint your original install used (see generate-cert.ps1|sh).

elements.name: secretsMode
elements.label: Tenant/app secret storage
elements.toolTip: MUST match your original install. If your original install used Azure Key Vault, picking Local database here will make the app unable to find secrets that only exist in that vault (SecretNotConfiguredException at runtime) — and vice versa.

elements.name: imageTag
elements.label: Version to install
elements.toolTip: The published version tag to deploy, listed newest-first with the date each was pushed to the registry. This is the only thing this wizard changes. NOTE: this dropdown is populated by publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1|sh at publish time (from `az acr repository show-tags`) - these placeholder tokens are only ever uploaded after that substitution runs.

options.text: This wizard changes only the application version — every field on the previous step must match your original install exactly (Postgres/Redis/secrets mode, storage redundancy, passwords/keys). It leaves container/database/cache SIZES at main.bicep's own defaults; if your original install customized those, use Step 4 (upgrade-resources) or the full Deploy-to-Azure wizard instead, or those will be reset to their defaults on this deploy. WAF and Seq are also left at their defaults (both off) — if either was enabled on the original install, use the full wizard instead so it isn't silently disabled.
